subject: Post-call: RTBF / purge playbook and backup constraints

Subject: Post-call: RTBF / purge playbook and backup constraints
Attachments: redwood_rtbf_playbook.pdf (pdf), data_retention_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi Elena — great to meet earlier. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Notes from the call:
- Requirement: Right-to-be-forgotten (PII delete) requests must be actionable via API and UI; median SLA target requested: 7 calendar days.
- Scope: user PII stored in primary DB + derived embeddings (search index).
- Backups: They cannot have guaranteed immediate deletion from backups; ask: acceptable max purge window? MediApps team signaled desire for shortest possible.
- Residency: Customer data must remain in US region; legal wants audit trail for deletions.

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- API endpoint for RTBF requests and an ops playbook for purging primary stores and indexes.
- Audit logs (immutable append-only) and a deletion event record for legal.
- Backups: incremental snapshots have a retention/rotation policy; full immutable cold snapshots may take longer to fully purge.

Requested next steps (proposed):
1) Rishi: capture a technical playbook that maps each store (primary DB, embeddings index, caches, logs, backups) to expected purge timelines and constraints.
2) Marissa/Jordan: prepare a summary for MEDIApps legal with attestation language and proposed SLA options (7 days / 30 days / 90 days).
3) Elena: confirm whether 7 days is a hard requirement or a preference; confirm whether there are specific systems we must integrate with (SFTP, internal ticketing).

I've attached a draft playbook and a matrix that Rishi can annotate with exact timelines. Can we aim to have a technical draft by end of day Friday (2026-06-19)? Also proposing a 30-minute follow-up next week to finalize the SLA option.

Thanks —

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- 7-day SLA: This is our target for surface systems (primary DB + search index). It is not negotiable for customer-facing deletes due to regulatory commitments in a couple of our markets.
- Backups: We understand technical constraints; for our compliance team, anything beyond 90 days for full purging from backups will be problematic. If some backup media requires a longer window, we need a compensating control and a written attestation.
- Auditability: We need a signed deletion manifest with timestamps and the hashes of records removed (or a comparable proof-of-deletion).
- Integration: We will manage RTBF intake in our ticketing system (Zendesk). Ideally we get an endpoint or webhook we can call that returns a unique request id which we can stash in the ticket.

If Redwood can commit to 7 days for primary + index and a maximum of 90 days for backup purge (or provide documented compensating controls and a remediation plan), we can move forward with the pilot.

Elena Rivera
Head of Privacy & Compliance | MediApps

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Rivera <elena.rivera@mediapps.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: RTBF / purge playbook and backup constraints

Hi all — thanks, looping in technical details below so legal/compliance teams have concrete language. I annotated the attached playbook and the retention matrix; summary here.

Technical summary (concise):
- Primary DB (Postgres): delete operations are executed immediately when RTBF is processed. Records removed from the active DB within the same transaction; dependent rows (derived data) are flagged and removed by a downstream job that runs within the RTBF process. Expected completion: within 24 hours for small volumes, within 7 calendar days for large/complex accounts.
- Embeddings / search index (Redis + vector store): we can remove vectors and associated metadata within 24–72 hours depending on batch windows. Index compaction occurs in the next maintenance window; for tight SLAs we can trigger a manual compaction as part of the RTBF workflow.
- Caches (edge + app): short TTLs; purge triggered on delete event.
- Logs / audit trails: immutable write-once logs cannot be retroactively modified; we will append a deletion event with the record identifiers, timestamps, and the operator id (this is the attestation you requested).
- Backups / snapshots: this is the main constraint. Our standard backup rotation is 90 days for incremental snapshots, and up to 180 days for retained full snapshots on cold storage (depending on the account's Dedicated vs Hosted profile). For Hosted customers we can offer a documented retention guarantee: either 90-day max purge or a custom plan for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Options to meet MediApps requirements:
A) Hosted + standard offering: commit to 90-day maximum for recovery media where feasible; provide compensating control (signed deletion manifest, periodic verification report).
B) Dedicated or Private: allow configurable snapshot lifecycle; we can enforce a 90-day max retention in a Dedicated pool with contractual SLA and provide monthly retention proofs.
C) Accelerated purge add-on: run an expedited cold-snapshot wipe that reduces the effective purge window to ~30–45 days for an additional operations/engineering fee; not all storage backends can guarantee immediate physical overwrite.

API / Operational hooks we can deliver quickly:
- RTBF API endpoint that returns a request_id and status updates (webhook optional).
- Deletion manifest: JSON manifest with record ids, delete timestamps, and a signed digest (HMAC) for legal verification.
- Audit trail export for a given request_id (CSV / JSON).

Risks / caveats (transparent):
- Legal-level proof-of-deletion for cold immutable backups requires a combination of manifest + storage-provider confirmation; in some cloud storage models physical media may persist until rotation.
- We can provide attestations and monthly verification reports; for full immediate physical purge you'd need private/dedicated deployment and potentially custom storage arrangements.

Actionables I will do by EOD Friday (2026-06-19):
- Populate the attached retention matrix with concrete timelines per store and example payload sizes.
- Draft example deletion-manifest schema.

If MediApps prioritizes 7-day primary + index and 90-day maximum for backups, option A with compensating controls looks feasible for Hosted. If they need absolute zero on backup retention, we should discuss Dedicated/Private.

—Rishi
